import json

             or ((cfg.get("features") or {}).get("allowed_geographies") or ["the region"])[0])

H = int(cfg["sample"].get("horizon", 12))

else:                                            # the example data: $ millions shown in billions

def read(*p):
    f = os.path.join(OUT, *p)
    return pd.read_csv(f) if os.path.exists(f) else pd.DataFrame()


comp = read("comparison", "1_model_comparison.csv")

oos_h = read("oos", "2_oos_by_horizon.csv")
dm = read("oos", "3_dm_tests_vs_benchmark.csv")
picks = read("oos", "4_drivers_by_origin.csv")
stab = read("oos", "5_driver_stability.csv")
hold = read("oos", "7_holdout.csv")

a2, a3, a4 = (read("screen_first", f) for f in ("A2_screen_best_per_variable.csv", "A3_clusters.csv", "A4_shortlist.csv"))

try:                                    # the concepts sheet of the literature workbook (or the old CSV table)

except Exception:

FAM_ORDER = ["Benchmark", "Data-driven", "Literature", "Hybrid", "Auto ARDL", "Same growth as a driver",
             "Horizon combination", "Regime switching", "Statistical time series", "Machine learning", "Deep learning",
             "AI foundation model"]
FAM_COL = {"Benchmark": "grey", "Data-driven": "teal", "Literature": "gold", "Hybrid": "green",
           "Machine learning": "purple", "AI foundation model": "red", "Look-ahead check": "C9D3DC",
           "Statistical time series": "orange", "Deep learning": "plum", "Regime switching": "sea",
           "Auto ARDL": "3B5BA5", "Same growth as a driver": "8A6D3B", "Horizon combination": "B5487A"}

ranking = (oos[oos["family"] != "Look-ahead check"] if HAVE_OOS else comp).copy()

ranking = ranking.drop(columns=["drivers"], errors="ignore").merge(mlist[["model", "drivers"]], on="model", how="left")


def n_variables(s):
    """Distinct macro variables a model uses, long-run (error-correction) variables included."""
    if not isinstance(s, str) or s == "(none)":
        return 0
    if "%" in s:
        return np.nan
    return len({d.replace("long run: ", "").split("|")[0].split(":")[0] for d in s.split(", ")})


ranking["n_vars"] = ranking["drivers"].map(n_variables)
ranking["single_equation"] = ranking["family"].isin(["Data-driven", "Literature", "Hybrid"]) & ranking["n_vars"].notna()
ranking = ranking.sort_values(f"avg_1_{HM}_pct").reset_index(drop=True)
within = ranking[ranking["single_equation"] & ranking["n_vars"].between(1, MAXV)]
REC = within.iloc[0] if len(within) else ranking.iloc[0]
BEST = ranking[ranking["family"] != "Benchmark"].iloc[0]
CHALL = BEST if BEST["model"] != REC["model"] else ranking[ranking["model"] != REC["model"]].iloc[0]
AR = ranking.set_index("model").loc["AR(1) benchmark"]


def pct(x, d=2):
    return f"{x:.{d}f}%"


def less(r, h=HM):
    return f"{(1 - r[f'avg_1_{h}_pct'] / AR[f'avg_1_{h}_pct']) * 100:.0f}%"


def esc(s):
    return str(s).replace("$", "\\$").replace("|", "\\|")


def short(f):
    if not isinstance(f, str) or "|" not in f:
        return str(f).replace("long run: ", "LR ").replace(":", " ")
    code, tr, lag = f.split("|")
    tr = {"dlog": "q/q", "yoy": "y/y", "dlog2": "2q", "acc": "accel.", "gap": "gap", "rdlog": "real q/q",
          "ryoy": "real y/y", "diff": "chg", "diff2": "2q chg", "diff4": "y/y chg", "lvl": "level", "rgap": "gap"}.get(tr, tr)
    return f"{code} {tr} {lag}"


def table(df, widths=None, floatfmt=".2f"):
    """Pipe table; `widths` sets relative column widths in PowerPoint."""
    df = df.copy()
    for c in df.columns:
        if df[c].dtype.kind == "f":
            df[c] = df[c].map(lambda v: "" if pd.isna(v) else format(v, floatfmt))
    widths = widths or [1] * df.shape[1]
    dashes = [max(3, int(round(120 * w / sum(widths)))) for w in widths]
    print("| " + " | ".join(esc(c) for c in df.columns) + " |")
    print("|" + "|".join("-" * d for d in dashes) + "|")
    for r in df.astype(str).values:
        print("| " + " | ".join(esc(v) for v in r) + " |")
    print()


def chart(cid, spec):
    """Write a native-chart spec and print its marker (drawn by style_deck.py)."""
    json.dump(spec, open(os.path.join(CH, f"{cid}.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8"), default=float)
    print(f"[[chart: {cid}]]\n")


def family_bar_spec(t, title):
    t = t.copy()
    t["fo"] = t["family"].map({f: i for i, f in enumerate(FAM_ORDER)}).fillna(99)
    t = t.sort_values(["fo", f"avg_1_{HM}_pct"])
    return {"type": "barh", "categories": list(t["model"]), "title": title, "legend": False,
            "series": [{"name": f"1–{HM} quarters", "values": [round(v, 3) for v in t[f"avg_1_{HM}_pct"]],
                        "colors": [FAM_COL.get(f, "teal") for f in t["family"]]}],
            "number_format": '0.00"%"', "axis_format": '0.0"%"', "cat_font_size": 8, "gap_width": 35, "y_min": 0}


headline = (f"Within {MAXV} variables, {REC['model']} cuts the {HM}-quarter error by {less(REC)}")
n_feat = len(read("screen_first", "A1_screen_all.csv"))
n_rel = forms["mnemonic"].nunique() if not forms.empty else 0
n_stat = forms[forms["stationary"]]["mnemonic"].nunique() if not forms.empty else 0
n_origins = picks["origin"].nunique() if not picks.empty else 0
n_lit_on = int((litstat["status"] == "in use").sum()) if not litstat.empty else 0
_s = cfg["sample"]
_step, _every = int(_s.get("backtest_step", 1)), int(_s.get("reestimate_every", 1))
bt_desc = (("Every quarter" if _step == 1 else f"Every {_step} quarters") + f" from {_s['backtest_start']}"
           + (f" to {_s['backtest_end']}" if _s.get("backtest_end") else "")
           + ("; re-estimated at every origin" if _every == 1 else
              "; re-estimated once a year (Q%d), coefficients kept for the other quarters" % int(_s.get("reestimate_quarter", 1))
              if _every == 4 else f"; re-estimated every {_every} quarters"))

# Methodology

## Six steps take `{python} macro_cols` series to a small, tested model

[[step: bullseye | 1. Target | Organic quarterly log change of the balance]]

[[step: exchange | 2. Transform | Up to 7 stationary forms, lags 0–4]]

[[step: filter | 3. Select | Screen first, or Elastic Net first]]

[[step: layers | 4. Group | Near-duplicates count as one signal]]

[[step: search | 5. Search | Every 1–3 driver combination under economic rules]]

[[step: check-double | 6. Validate | Backtest, re-selection test, scenarios]]

[[band: Guiding principle | theory sets the rules (channels, signs, geography); data does the measuring (series, form, lag); the final ranking is on out-of-sample accuracy]]

## The target is the organic `{python} CHANGE` of the `{python} TARGET`, cleaned of one-off events

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column}
[[split: 40]]

**Target variable**

y~t~ = ln[(L~t~ − A~t~) / L~t−1~]

- L~t~ is the quarter-end balance; A~t~ removes acquisitions and portfolio sales
- The balance is not stationary; its log change is
- Each COVID quarter (2020Q1–2021Q2) has its own dummy and is left out of the error
:::

::: {.column}
```{python}

lv = level / SCALE
chart("balance", {"type": "line", "markers": False, "categories": [str(p) for p in lv.index],
                  "series": [{"name": TARGET.capitalize(), "values": [round(v, 2) for v in lv.values], "color": "teal"}],
                  "title": f"Reported {TARGET} ({UNITS})", "legend": False, "number_format": "0",
                  "label_skip": 16})
```
:::

::::

## Each variable is tried in several economically meaningful forms

[[card: Levels (indexes, \$, counts) | q/q, y/y and 2-quarter growth; Acceleration of y/y growth; % gap from 3-year average; Real growth, deflated by CPI]]

[[card: Rates (%, pp) | q/q, 2-quarter and y/y change; Level, if stationary; Gap from 3-year average]]

[[card*: Constructed variables | Real 5-year mortgage rate; Mortgage spread over 5-year GoC; Term spread (10-year minus overnight)]]

[[band: Only stationary forms are kept | every window looks backwards only; ADF test on each form; lags 0–4 give `{python} f"{n_feat:,}"` candidate features]]

[[icon@gold: filter | Relevance | `{python} ' and '.join(map(str, cfg['features'].get('allowed_geographies') or ['All']))` series; industry detail dropped]]

[[icon@gold: check | Screen | p < 0.05 and the expected sign, controlling for momentum and COVID]]

[[icon@gold: layers | Cluster | Correlation above 0.75 counts as one signal; `{python} REGION` preferred]]

[[icon@gold: search | Search | Best 1–3 driver combination by out-of-sample error]]
:::

::::

## Two ways to choose the drivers, then the same final search

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column}
**A. Screen first**

1. Each candidate alone in y~t~ = a + ρy~t−1~ + dummies + βz~t~
2. Pass: p < 0.05 and expected sign: `{python} int(a2["passed"].sum()) if not a2.empty else "–"` variables
3. Cluster: `{python} a3["cluster"].nunique() if not a3.empty else "–"` groups, shortlist of `{python} len(a4)`
4. Final search
:::

::: {.column}
**B. Elastic Net first** (glmnet conventions)

1. Momentum and dummies unpenalised; signs constrained
2. λ set so 10 features enter; deterministic
3. Kept if chosen in ≥ 60% of 100 subsamples: `{python} len(b3) if not b3.empty else "–"` features
4. Group, then the same final search
:::

::::

## Selection rules keep every model economic, simple and accurate

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column}
[[split: 46]]

**Each candidate on its own**

y~t~ = α + ρ·y~t−1~ + Σ γ~q~·D~q,t~ + β·z~t−ℓ~ + ε~t~

- z is one variable in one form; ℓ is its lag (0–4)
- Lagged growth and COVID dummies are controls
- Pass: p < 0.05 (Newey-West) and the expected sign
:::

::: {.column}
[[icon@green: check | Every driver significant | Robust t-statistic above 1.96]]

[[icon@green: balance | Every sign as expected | Explainable to the business and the regulator]]

[[icon@green: compress | No strong collinearity | VIF below 5; one driver per economic theme]]

[[icon@green: chart-line | Ranked out of sample | Balance error over `{python} H` quarters; simplest within 5% wins]]
:::

::::

## The literature points to four channels for household credit

[[icon: home | House prices | Collateral value and the size of mortgages. Hofmann (2004); Goodhart & Hofmann (2008); Muellbauer et al. (2015)]]

[[icon: wallet | Household income | Borrowing capacity. Fitzpatrick & McQuinn (2007); Muellbauer, St-Amant & Williams (2015)]]

[[icon: percent | Cost of credit | Mortgage rates, slow pass-through via 5-year renewals. Calza et al. (2003); Godbout, Xu & Su (2025)]]

[[icon: user-tie | Labour market | Unemployment and income risk. Included in the ECB BEAST credit-demand block (Budnik et al. 2023)]]

[[band: Also in the literature | real GDP and the policy rate (Hofmann 2004; Guo & Stepanyan 2011); inflation and the term spread have no clear sign]]

## The literature table: drivers of household credit and our series

```{python}
#| output: asis
if not littab.empty:
    t = littab.copy()
    st = litstat.set_index("concept_id")["status"] if not litstat.empty else pd.Series(dtype=str)
    t["Effect"] = t["effect_on_loan_growth"].map({"Positive": "Positive", "Negative": "Negative", "Ambiguous": "Ambiguous"})
    t["Evidence"] = t["evidence"].str.replace(r"\s*\(([^)]*?:[^)]*)\)", "", regex=True).map(
        lambda s: "; ".join(x.strip() for x in str(s).split(";")[:3]) + (" …" if len(str(s).split(";")) > 3 else ""))
    t["Our series"] = t["series_name"].fillna("—")
    t["Status"] = t["concept_id"].map(st).fillna("").str.replace(" (not used by a model)", "", regex=False)
    t = t[["concept", "Effect", "Evidence", "Our series", "Status"]]
    t.columns = ["Concept", "Effect", "Evidence", "Our series", "Status"]
    table(t, [2.2, 1.2, 5.2, 1.6, 1.6])
```

::: notes
The table is the 'concepts' sheet of the literature workbook (full references in its 'references' sheet). Models refer to concepts, not series names: map each concept to your series in the series_name column, and set include = no to drop a concept you do not believe from every literature and hybrid model.
:::

ICON = {"Benchmark": "flag", "Data-driven": "database", "Literature": "book", "Hybrid": "balance",
        "Machine learning": "brain", "AI foundation model": "robot", "Statistical time series": "wave",
        "Deep learning": "layers", "Regime switching": "exchange", "Auto ARDL": "search",
        "Same growth as a driver": "percent", "Horizon combination": "calendar"}
COLR = {"Benchmark": "grey", "Data-driven": "", "Literature": "gold", "Hybrid": "green",
        "Machine learning": "purple", "AI foundation model": "red", "Statistical time series": "orange",
        "Deep learning": "plum", "Regime switching": "sea", "Auto ARDL": "3B5BA5", "Same growth as a driver": "8A6D3B",
        "Horizon combination": "B5487A"}
for f in FAM_ORDER:
    ms = mlist[mlist["family"] == f]["model"].map(lambda m: m.split(": ")[-1]).tolist()
    if not ms and f != "AI foundation model":

    ms = [m.replace("Same growth as ", "").replace("Personal disposable income", "income") for m in ms]

    c = f"@{COLR.get(f, '')}" if COLR.get(f) else ""
    print(f"[[icon{c}: {ICON.get(f, 'cogs')} | {f} | {esc(body)}]]\n")

::::

::: notes
All five use the literature core drivers, so their errors compare directly with the four-channel core. Markov switching infers two unobserved regimes (low and high mean growth) and carries their probabilities forward; the threshold and smooth-transition models switch on the house price growth path, so a scenario can move them into the other regime; the time-varying model lets coefficients drift slowly; the break-adaptive model re-estimates after a detected structural break. Errors shown are the average over 1–12 quarters on the same basis as the ranking.
:::

## Machine learning and AI: what they add, and what they cost

| Model | Inputs | Responds to scenarios | Run time |
|------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|-------------------|
| Ridge regression | Momentum, dummies, pooled drivers (literature core + data-chosen) | Yes | Seconds |
| Random forest, gradient boosting | Same | Yes, within the historical range | ~10 s each |
| Neural network (5 small nets, averaged) | Same | Yes | ~10 s |
| ARIMAX, Theta | Literature drivers with ARMA errors; Theta: own history only | ARIMAX yes, Theta no | Seconds |
| TiDE (Google, 2023), TFT (2021) | Own history, literature drivers and their scenario paths | Yes | TiDE ~1.5 min, TFT ~4 min |
| N-HiTS (2023) | Own history and the drivers as past inputs | Only beyond the first 4 quarters | ~1 min per run |
| Chronos-Bolt (Amazon, 2024) | Own history only | No: same path in every scenario | < 1 s per forecast |
| Chronos-2 (Amazon, 2025) | Own history, literature drivers and their scenario paths | Yes | < 1 s per forecast |

::: notes
Fixed hyperparameters, no tuning loop; machine-learning and deep-learning models are re-estimated once a year. The deep networks are kept small (a few thousand weights) because we have about 100 quarters; each is the average of 3 random seeds. Foundation models are not trained on our data, so they measure how much bank-specific modelling adds.
:::

## Every model is tested the same way, 4, 8 and 12 quarters ahead

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column}
**Rolling backtest**

- `{python} bt_desc`: forecast 1–`{python} H` quarters with realised macro values
- Error on the balance level; COVID windows left out
- Drivers chosen once with all the data, so optimistic
:::

::: {.column}
★ **True out-of-sample test**

- At `{python} n_origins` origins, the whole selection is re-run with data up to the origin
- Compared at 4, 8 and 12 quarters ahead
- Diebold-Mariano tests against AR(1); holdout of the last `{python} cfg["oos"]["holdout_quarters"]` quarters
:::

::: {.column}
**Why the two rankings differ**

The rolling backtest keeps the drivers chosen with all the data, so data-driven models look better than they are.

The out-of-sample test re-chooses everything at each origin. Decisions use that test.

## The best model of each family at 4, 8 and 12 quarters

```{python}
#| output: asis
rows = []
for f in FAM_ORDER:
    d = ranking[ranking["family"] == f]
    if d.empty:
        continue
    r = d.iloc[0]
    row = {"Family": f, "Best model": r["model"].split(": ")[-1]}
    for h in HZ:
        row[f"1–{h}q"] = pct(r[f"avg_1_{h}_pct"])
    row[f"vs AR(1), 1–{HM}q"] = "" if f == "Benchmark" else f"{less(r)} less"
    if not dm.empty and f != "Benchmark":
        s = dm[(dm["model"] == r["model"]) & (dm["horizon_q"] == min(HZ))]
        row[f"Beats AR(1) at {min(HZ)}q (DM 5%)"] = ("yes" if bool(s["better_than_benchmark_at_5pct"].iloc[0]) else "no") if len(s) else ""
    rows.append(row)
t = pd.DataFrame(rows).fillna("")
table(t, [1.7, 3] + [1] * len(HZ) + [1.4] + ([1.6] if t.shape[1] > len(HZ) + 3 else []))
```

::: notes
Average balance error over 1 to h quarters, COVID windows excluded, `{python} basis`. Diebold-Mariano test with the small-sample correction; at 8 and 12 quarters there are too few independent origins for a reliable test.
:::

if r is not None and pd.notna(r.get("n_obs", np.nan)):
    tests = [("Driver significance", "max p-value of drivers", lambda v: v < 0.05, "Largest p-value"),
             ("Multicollinearity", "max VIF", lambda v: v < 5, "Largest VIF"),
             ("Autocorrelation", "Ljung-Box p (4)", lambda v: v > 0.05, "Ljung-Box p, 4 lags"),
             ("Autocorrelation", "Ljung-Box p (8)", lambda v: v > 0.05, "Ljung-Box p, 8 lags"),
             ("Heteroskedasticity", "Breusch-Pagan p", lambda v: v > 0.05, "Breusch-Pagan p"),
             ("Normality", "Jarque-Bera p", lambda v: v > 0.05, "Jarque-Bera p"),
             ("Stability", "CUSUM p", lambda v: v > 0.05, "CUSUM p")]
    rows = [{"Check": a, "Test": t, "Result": f"{r[c]:.3f}", "Pass": "Pass" if ok(r[c]) else "Review"}
            for a, c, ok, t in tests if c in r and pd.notna(r[c])]
    rows.append({"Check": "Economic sense", "Test": "Signs as expected", "Result": str(r["wrong-sign drivers"]),
                 "Pass": "Pass" if r["wrong-sign drivers"] == "none" else "Review"})
    table(pd.DataFrame(rows), [2, 2.2, 1, 0.8])

```{python}
#| include: false
# Scenario order check that works with any scenario names: each name is ranked by keywords
# (severe/stress < downside/adverse < baseline < upside); names without a keyword are left out of the check.
def severity(name):
    n = str(name).lower()
    for words, rank in ((("severe", "stress", "extreme", "tail"), -2), (("downside", "adverse", "pessimistic", "down"), -1),
                        (("upside", "optimistic", "upper", "strong"), 1), (("baseline", "base", "central", "reference"), 0)):
        if any(w in n for w in words):
            return rank
    return None


v_ = yearend[yearend["model"] == REC["model"]]
ranked = sorted([(severity(c), c) for c in v_.columns if c not in ("model", "date") and severity(c) is not None])
pairs = [(a, b) for (ra, a), (rb, b) in zip(ranked, ranked[1:]) if ra < rb]
SC_OK = all(bool((v_[a] <= v_[b] + 1e-9).all()) for a, b in pairs) if pairs else None
ORDER_TXT = " ≤ ".join(c for _, c in ranked) if len(ranked) > 1 else "only one scenario"
SC_TITLE = ("All scenarios are ordered sensibly" if SC_OK else
            "Scenario order needs a review" if SC_OK is False else "Forecasts under each scenario")
```

## Known limitations and how they are managed

[[icon@red: crosshairs | Conditional accuracy | Tests use realised macro values; live error adds scenario forecast error]]

[[icon@red: compress | Small sample | About 95 quarters: sign priors, grouping and re-selection limit overfitting]]

[[icon@red: random | Drivers move with the data | Re-selection test and stability table; theory-anchored challengers]]

[[icon@red: coins | Credit aggregates as drivers | Mortgage-credit growth is close to the target: review or exclude that theme]]

[[icon@red: robot | Machine learning and AI | Less transparent; trees cannot extrapolate in severe scenarios]]

[[icon@red: database | `{python} "Simulated data" if simulated else "Data"` | `{python} "All figures must be re-run on actual bank and macro scenario data" if simulated else "Results reflect the data supplied"`]]
